retained_structural_inputs.statement: Exact generic-pencil degree identity and equal-genus one-puncture inverse certificate; all finite-image punctures retained.
Actual rank-one embedding makes K a closed immersion on its radical zero curve.
Descended trace gives full reduced-curve isomorphism and under hypothetical failure every target component has affine normalization A1.
No abelian Galois intermediate, square-free source pullbacks, divisor domination and denominator removal.
Noncomposite polynomial gives geometrically integral generic fibre by the retained field-agnostic argument.

direct_proof_arguments: An irreducible plane equation is noncomposite, so its generic fibre is geometrically integral and Vistoli applies.
The one-place condition is intrinsic to the smooth completion of the affine normalization, independent of its plane embedding.
The integral compactification dominates A1; its coordinate rings are torsion-free C[t]-modules, hence filtered unions of free modules and flat.
The special proper fibre adds one smooth point, so its normalization sequence gives arithmetic genus g0 plus the finite intrinsic normalization deficit delta.
Proper flat Euler-characteristic constancy gives the generic genus G=g0+delta and the one-puncture property.
A curve isomorphism preserves its normalized projective genus and finite quotient length, so no ambient extension is required to match generic pencil invariants.
Full inverse-image support and square-free Keller pullback give b(K)=c g; the retained one-puncture degree identity forces d=1.
Any positive-power descent of the normal trace gives a cyclic source intermediate field, excluded by HW0; denominator removal makes the normal trace target-polynomial.
The actual descended radical curve is an entire reduced-curve isomorphism, and hypothetical failure makes each target component A1-normalized, so the one-place inverse theorem closes every component.
A remaining one-place radical component must have an additional source prime over its image outside the entire radical curve; injectivity on that curve excludes a second such component within it.
